claim: MG2I produces singlet oxygen when bound to the fluorogen-activating protein dL5** and exposed to far-red light.
source: MG2I, a chemical fluorogen, produces singlet oxygen when bound to the fluorogen-activating protein dL5** and exposed to far-red light.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work (He et al., 2016) showing the photosensitizer properties of the dL5**-MG2I complex.

claim: Transgenic zebrafish expressing dL5** within neuronal mitochondria showed dramatic MG2I- and light-dependent neurobehavioral deficits.
source: Transgenic zebrafish expressing dL5** within neuronal mitochondria showed dramatic MG2I- and light-dependent neurobehavioral deficits, caused by neuronal bioenergetic crisis and acute neuronal depolarization.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Neurobehavioral deficits in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish were caused by neuronal bioenergetic crisis and acute neuronal depolarization.
source: Transgenic zebrafish expressing dL5** within neuronal mitochondria showed dramatic MG2I- and light-dependent neurobehavioral deficits, caused by neuronal bioenergetic crisis and acute neuronal depolarization.
evidence: The abstract states this causal relationship, which is supported by ATP measurements (Figure 4A), oxygen consumption data (Figure 4C-E), and electrophysiology recordings (Figure 3).

claim: The neurobehavioral abnormalities resulted from loss of neuronal respiration.
source: These abnormalities resulted from loss of neuronal respiration, associated with mitochondrial fragmentation, swelling and elimination of cristae.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by oxygen consumption rate measurements (Figure 4C-G) and electron microscopy data (Figure 5E-G).

claim: Loss of neuronal respiration was associated with mitochondrial fragmentation, swelling and elimination of cristae.
source: These abnormalities resulted from loss of neuronal respiration, associated with mitochondrial fragmentation, swelling and elimination of cristae.
evidence: The abstract states this association, which is supported by confocal microscopy (Figure 5A-D) and transmission electron microscopy (Figure 5E-G) showing mitochondrial structural changes.

claim: Remaining cellular ultrastructure was preserved initially after mitochondrial damage.
source: Remaining cellular ultrastructure was preserved initially, but cellular pathology downstream of mitochondrial damage eventually culminated in neuronal death.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by electron microscopy images (Figure 6E) showing normal nuclear membrane, Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum immediately after light exposure despite severe mitochondrial damage.

claim: Cellular pathology downstream of mitochondrial damage eventually culminated in neuronal death.
source: Remaining cellular ultrastructure was preserved initially, but cellular pathology downstream of mitochondrial damage eventually culminated in neuronal death.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by acridine orange labeling showing increased cell death at 24 hours post-exposure (Figure 6C-D) and electron microscopy showing apoptotic bodies (Figure 6E).

claim: The dL5**-MG2I complex shows maximal excitation in the far-red light range.
source: The dL5**-MG2I complex showed maximal excitation in the highly tissue-penetrant far-red light range, and produced singlet oxygen (1O2, molecular dioxygen in its first electronically excited state) through inter-system crossing, with high quantum yield and with little photobleaching (He et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to He et al., 2016, and by spectral data shown in Figure 1H and Table 1.

claim: The dL5**-MG2I complex produces singlet oxygen through inter-system crossing with high quantum yield and little photobleaching.
source: The dL5**-MG2I complex showed maximal excitation in the highly tissue-penetrant far-red light range, and produced singlet oxygen (1O2, molecular dioxygen in its first electronically excited state) through inter-system crossing, with high quantum yield and with little photobleaching (He et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to He et al., 2016.

claim: Neither dL5** nor MG2I alone produces detectable singlet oxygen under far-red illumination.
source: Importantly, neither dL5** nor MG2I alone produced detectable 1O2 under far-red illumination, and the dL5**-MG2I complex did not produce 1O2 in the absence of light.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to He et al., 2016, and by control experiments shown in Figure 2 where either MG2I or dL5** alone did not cause phenotypes.

claim: The dL5**-MG2I complex does not produce singlet oxygen in the absence of light.
source: Importantly, neither dL5** nor MG2I alone produced detectable 1O2 under far-red illumination, and the dL5**-MG2I complex did not produce 1O2 in the absence of light.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to He et al., 2016, and by control experiments shown in Figure 2 where no light exposure did not cause phenotypes in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish.

claim: Singlet oxygen has a lifetime of approximately 4μs in water.
source: 1O2 is highly reactive with organic molecules and thus reacts within a short radius (<20 nm) of its site of formation in living systems (its lifetime is approximately 4μs in water [Wilkinson et al., 1995], but may be as low as 100ns in cells [Moan and Berg, 1991]).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Wilkinson et al., 1995.

claim: Singlet oxygen lifetime may be as low as 100ns in cells.
source: 1O2 is highly reactive with organic molecules and thus reacts within a short radius (<20 nm) of its site of formation in living systems (its lifetime is approximately 4μs in water [Wilkinson et al., 1995], but may be as low as 100ns in cells [Moan and Berg, 1991]).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Moan and Berg, 1991.

claim: Singlet oxygen reacts within a short radius (<20 nm) of its site of formation in living systems.
source: 1O2 is highly reactive with organic molecules and thus reacts within a short radius (<20 nm) of its site of formation in living systems (its lifetime is approximately 4μs in water [Wilkinson et al., 1995], but may be as low as 100ns in cells [Moan and Berg, 1991]).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is inferred from the short lifetime of singlet oxygen cited from Wilkinson et al., 1995 and Moan and Berg, 1991.

claim: dL5** fused to TRF1 was used to induce 8-oxoguanine formation specifically in telomeric DNA of cultured cells.
source: For example, dL5** fused to TRF1, a component of the shelterin complex, was employed recently to induce 8-oxoguanine formation specifically in the telomeric DNA of cultured cells (Fouquerel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Fouquerel et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment of HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5** with MG2I and far-red light resulted in decreased oxygen consumption.
source: Treatment of these cells with MG2I and exposure to far-red light resulted in decreased oxygen consumption, loss of respiratory chain activity, mitochondrial depolarization, compensatory glycolysis, and secondary ROS generation that was sufficient to cause oxidative telomere damage and cell cycle arrest (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment of HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5** with MG2I and far-red light resulted in loss of respiratory chain activity.
source: Treatment of these cells with MG2I and exposure to far-red light resulted in decreased oxygen consumption, loss of respiratory chain activity, mitochondrial depolarization, compensatory glycolysis, and secondary ROS generation that was sufficient to cause oxidative telomere damage and cell cycle arrest (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment of HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5** with MG2I and far-red light resulted in mitochondrial depolarization.
source: Treatment of these cells with MG2I and exposure to far-red light resulted in decreased oxygen consumption, loss of respiratory chain activity, mitochondrial depolarization, compensatory glycolysis, and secondary ROS generation that was sufficient to cause oxidative telomere damage and cell cycle arrest (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment of HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5** with MG2I and far-red light resulted in compensatory glycolysis.
source: Treatment of these cells with MG2I and exposure to far-red light resulted in decreased oxygen consumption, loss of respiratory chain activity, mitochondrial depolarization, compensatory glycolysis, and secondary ROS generation that was sufficient to cause oxidative telomere damage and cell cycle arrest (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment of HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5** with MG2I and far-red light resulted in secondary ROS generation sufficient to cause oxidative telomere damage and cell cycle arrest.
source: Treatment of these cells with MG2I and exposure to far-red light resulted in decreased oxygen consumption, loss of respiratory chain activity, mitochondrial depolarization, compensatory glycolysis, and secondary ROS generation that was sufficient to cause oxidative telomere damage and cell cycle arrest (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: Neurons are generally dependent on mitochondrial function for ATP generation.
source: Unlike transformed cells in culture, however, neurons are generally dependent on mitochondrial function for ATP generation (reviewed in Van Laar and Berman, 2013) and this is known to influence the responses of neuronal mitochondria to perturbing stimuli (Van Laar et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to Van Laar and Berman, 2013 and Van Laar et al., 2011.

claim: Neuronal dependence on mitochondrial function influences the responses of neuronal mitochondria to perturbing stimuli.
source: Unlike transformed cells in culture, however, neurons are generally dependent on mitochondrial function for ATP generation (reviewed in Van Laar and Berman, 2013) and this is known to influence the responses of neuronal mitochondria to perturbing stimuli (Van Laar et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Van Laar et al., 2011.

claim: Double transgenic NeuMitoFAP zebrafish showed strong mCerulean3 expression throughout the nervous system.
source: Double transgenic Tg(eno2:gal4FF)pt425; Tg(UAS:COX4-COX8-dL5**-mCer3)pt427 zebrafish (referred to as 'NeuMitoFAP' zebrafish for brevity) showed strong mCerulean3 expression throughout the nervous system (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by epifluorescence images in Figure 1C showing mCerulean3 expression in the telencephalon, midbrain, hindbrain, spinal cord, retina, and enteric nervous system.

claim: Punctate mCerulean3-labeled structures corresponding to individual mitochondria were visible within axons of live NeuMitoFAP larval neurons.
source: At high magnification, punctate mCerulean3-labeled structures corresponding to individual mitochondria were visible within axons of live NeuMitoFAP larval neurons (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by confocal microscopy images in Figure 1D showing individual mitochondria in the lateral line nerve.

claim: mCerulean3 co-localized extensively with TOM20 in CNS neurons of NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
source: Tissue sections revealed extensive co-localization of mCerulean3 with TOM20 (a mitochondrial marker) in CNS neurons of NeuMitoFAP zebrafish (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1E and quantitative colocalization analysis in Figure 1F-G.

claim: The mCerulean3 signal correlated strongly with the mitochondrial TOM20 signal but not with the nuclear DAPI signal.
source: Pixel-by-pixel analysis of single confocal planes showed that the mCerulean3 signal correlated strongly with the mitochondrial TOM20 signal, but not with the nuclear DAPI signal (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by scatter plot analysis (Figure 1F) and Pearson correlation coefficients (Figure 1G) showing high correlation with TOM20 and low correlation with DAPI.

claim: dL5**-mCerulean3 is expressed in the neuronal mitochondria of NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
source: These data show that dL5**-mCerulean3 is expressed in the neuronal mitochondria of NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by the colocalization data with TOM20 (Figure 1E-G) and the punctate mitochondrial morphology (Figure 1D).

claim: All four experimental groups showed normal motor activity at 5dpf prior to far-red light exposure.
source: Zebrafish from all four experimental groups showed normal motor activity (Figure 2B) and morphology (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) at 5dpf.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by swimming traces in Figure 2B (pre-exposure) and VMR data in Figure 2C (upper graphs).

claim: Robust responses to abrupt green light-dark transitions were apparent in all four experimental groups prior to far-red light exposure.
source: Robust responses to abrupt green light – dark transitions were apparent in all four experimental groups (Figure 2B, left panel; Figure 2C, upper graphs) prior to far-red light exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by VMR traces in Figure 2C (upper graphs) showing similar responses in all groups before light exposure.

claim: Motor responses were eliminated acutely in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish following exposure to 60 J/cm2 far-red light.
source: However, motor responses were eliminated acutely in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish, but not controls, following exposure to 60 J/cm2 far-red light (mean ± SE swimming speed in dark phase of VMR, pre- versus post-exposure: WT, 1.80 ± 0.10 vs. 1.70 ± 0.08 mm/s; WT-MG2I, 1.69 ± 0.09 vs. 1.60 ± 0.10 mm/s; NeuMitoFAP, 2.02 ± 0.10 vs. 2.13 ± 0.08 mm/s; NeuMitoFAP-MG2I 2.36 ± 0.09 vs. 0.08 ± 0.02 mm/s, p<10−15, 2-way ANOVA with Šidák multiple comparisons test; Figure 2B-D; Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by swimming traces (Figure 2B), VMR graphs (Figure 2C), and quantification (Figure 2D).

claim: Loss of motor function in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish was dependent on the amount of light energy delivered.
source: Loss of motor function in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish was dependent on the amount of light energy delivered (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), but independent of the rate of delivery between 16–160 mW/cm2 at a fixed total exposure of 60 J/cm2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by dose-response data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing progressive loss of motor function with increasing light doses.

claim: Loss of motor function in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish was independent of the rate of light delivery between 16–160 mW/cm2 at a fixed total exposure of 60 J/cm2.
source: Loss of motor function in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish was dependent on the amount of light energy delivered (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), but independent of the rate of delivery between 16–160 mW/cm2 at a fixed total exposure of 60 J/cm2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 showing similar motor deficits at different power densities delivering the same total energy.

claim: Heart rate and circulation were preserved in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light despite loss of motor function.
source: Although NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light lost spontaneous and evoked motor function, their heart rate and circulation were preserved (Figure 2E; Video 2) and there were no gross morphological changes (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), showing that the larvae remained alive and that abnormalities were restricted to the nervous system.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by heart rate measurements (Figure 2E) and videomicrography (Video 2) showing normal cardiac function.

claim: There were no gross morphological changes in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light.
source: Although NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light lost spontaneous and evoked motor function, their heart rate and circulation were preserved (Figure 2E; Video 2) and there were no gross morphological changes (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), showing that the larvae remained alive and that abnormalities were restricted to the nervous system.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by transmitted light micrographs in Figure 2—figure supplement 4 showing normal morphology.

claim: The dramatic neurological phenotype was dependent on all three components of the chemoptogenetic system (far-red light exposure in the presence of both dL5** and MG2I).
source: Together, these data show a dramatic neurological phenotype that was dependent on all three components of the chemoptogenetic system (far-red light exposure in the presence of both dL5** and MG2I), and therefore attributable to 1O2 formation at the site of dL5** expression in neuronal mitochondria.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by control experiments showing no phenotype when any component is missing (Figure 2B-D).

claim: The neurological phenotype is attributable to singlet oxygen formation at the site of dL5** expression in neuronal mitochondria.
source: Together, these data show a dramatic neurological phenotype that was dependent on all three components of the chemoptogenetic system (far-red light exposure in the presence of both dL5** and MG2I), and therefore attributable to 1O2 formation at the site of dL5** expression in neuronal mitochondria.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is inferred from the requirement of all three components (dL5**, MG2I, and far-red light) which are known to produce singlet oxygen when combined.

claim: The severity of the abnormalities was determined by the amount of far-red light energy delivered.
source: Furthermore, the severity of the abnormalities was determined by the amount of far-red light energy delivered.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by dose-response data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lateral line sensory neurons in control zebrafish showed similar stable baseline membrane potentials that changed minimally during 20-30 min of far-red light exposure.
source: In control zebrafish, lateral line sensory neurons showed similar stable baseline membrane potentials that changed minimally during 20–30 min of far-red light exposure (baseline versus final membrane potential: WT-MG2I, −66.9 ± 1.4 vs. −63.2 ± 1.2 mV; NeuMitoFAP, −64.4 ± 1.2 vs. −60.8 ± 2.5 mV; mean ± SE; Figure 3A-C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with quantitative data and supported by electrophysiology traces in Figure 3A and quantification in Figure 3B-C.

claim: Sensory neurons in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae showed similar baseline membrane potential to controls but depolarized progressively during exposure to far-red light.
source: Sensory neurons in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae showed similar baseline membrane potential to controls but depolarized progressively during exposure to far-red light, initially reaching threshold potential and firing high-frequency trains of action potentials, then depolarizing further to become refractory (baseline versus final membrane potential −60.8 ± 2.4 mV vs. −29.4 ± 4.5 mV, p<0.0001, 2-way ANOVA with Tukey multiple comparison test; Figure 3A-C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by electrophysiology traces in Figure 3A showing progressive depolarization and action potentials.

claim: NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons initially reached threshold potential and fired high-frequency trains of action potentials during far-red light exposure.
source: Sensory neurons in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae showed similar baseline membrane potential to controls but depolarized progressively during exposure to far-red light, initially reaching threshold potential and firing high-frequency trains of action potentials, then depolarizing further to become refractory (baseline versus final membrane potential −60.8 ± 2.4 mV vs. −29.4 ± 4.5 mV, p<0.0001, 2-way ANOVA with Tukey multiple comparison test; Figure 3A-C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electrophysiology traces in Figure 3A showing action potential firing during depolarization.

claim: Phosphocreatine prevented depolarization of NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons during far-red light exposure.
source: The baseline resting membrane potential was unaltered by phosphocreatine, but its presence prevented depolarization of NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons during far-red light exposure (baseline versus final membrane potential: −62.7 ± 1.4 vs. −59.6 ± 2.8 mV; Figure 3A-C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electrophysiology traces in Figure 3A and quantification in Figure 3B-C showing stable membrane potential with phosphocreatine.

claim: 10/10 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons depolarized by ≥20% of their baseline membrane potential following a mean exposure of 44.3 ± 6.3 J/cm2 far-red light.
source: Overall, 10/10 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons depolarized by ≥20% of their baseline membrane potential following a mean exposure of 44.3 ± 6.3 J/cm2 far-red light, whereas in the presence of phosphocreatine, only 1/6 neurons depolarized after exposure to >80 J/cm2 (p=0.0014, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: In the presence of phosphocreatine, only 1/6 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons depolarized after exposure to >80 J/cm2 far-red light.
source: Overall, 10/10 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons depolarized by ≥20% of their baseline membrane potential following a mean exposure of 44.3 ± 6.3 J/cm2 far-red light, whereas in the presence of phosphocreatine, only 1/6 neurons depolarized after exposure to >80 J/cm2 (p=0.0014, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: The acute neurological deficits in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish were caused by neuronal depolarization resulting from depletion of ATP.
source: Together, these data show that the acute neurological deficits provoked in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish by exposure to far-red light were caused by neuronal depolarization, resulting from depletion of ATP that is necessary to drive the active ionic transporters that maintain transmembrane ionic gradients underlying the resting membrane potential.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by electrophysiology data showing depolarization (Figure 3A-C) and rescue by phosphocreatine which provides ATP (Figure 3A-D).

claim: ATP is necessary to drive the active ionic transporters that maintain transmembrane ionic gradients underlying the resting membrane potential.
source: Together, these data show that the acute neurological deficits provoked in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish by exposure to far-red light were caused by neuronal depolarization, resulting from depletion of ATP that is necessary to drive the active ionic transporters that maintain transmembrane ionic gradients underlying the resting membrane potential.
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents established knowledge about neuronal physiology.

claim: Far-red light exposure caused a ≈10% decrease in whole animal ATP content in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae.
source: A bioluminescence assay was used to measure ATP concentration in lysates from NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae. Far-red light exposure caused a ≈10% decrease in whole animal ATP content (pre-light 4.12 ± 0.10 vs. post-light 3.69 ± 0.11 μMol ATP/g protein; mean ± SE; p=0.0060, 2-tailed t-test; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by ATP measurements in Figure 4A.

claim: NeuMitoFAP zebrafish exposed to far-red light in the presence of MG2I showed a ≈24% decrease in whole larval oxygen consumption rate compared with controls not treated with MG2I.
source: NeuMitoFAP zebrafish exposed to far-red light in the presence of MG2I showed a ≈24% decrease in whole larval OCR compared with controls that were not treated with MG2I (NeuMitoFAP 170.7 ± 8.9 vs. NeuMitoFAP-MG2I 129.2 ± 7.0 pMol/min; mean ±SE; p=0.00053, unpaired t-test; Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by oxygen consumption measurements in Figure 4C-D.

claim: WT controls exposed to far-red light showed similar stable oxygen consumption rates regardless of MG2I treatment.
source: In contrast, WT controls exposed to far-red light showed similar stable OCRs regardless of MG2I treatment (WT, 194.8 ± 11.4; WT-MG2I, 189.1 ± 14.1 pMol/min; mean ± SE; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by oxygen consumption measurements in Figure 4E.

claim: Bath acidification rate was unaltered in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light.
source: Bath acidification rate was unaltered in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), providing no evidence of compensatory glycolysis following abrogation of neuronal mitochondrial function.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by bath acidification rate measurements in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: There was no evidence of compensatory glycolysis following abrogation of neuronal mitochondrial function in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish.
source: Bath acidification rate was unaltered in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish exposed to far-red light (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), providing no evidence of compensatory glycolysis following abrogation of neuronal mitochondrial function.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is inferred from the lack of change in bath acidification rate, which would increase with glycolysis.

claim: NeuMitoFAP-MG2I dissociated brain cells showed a dramatic, far-red light dose-dependent decrease in maximal respiration.
source: Under these conditions, NeuMitoFAP-MG2I cells, but not controls, showed a dramatic, far-red light dose-dependent, decrease in maximal respiration (measured by comparing OCR following exposure to the uncoupling agent FCCP with OCR following exposure to the complex I and III inhibitors rotenone and antimycin-A; Figure 4F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Seahorse measurements in Figure 4F-G showing dose-dependent decrease in maximal respiration.

claim: The combination of MG2I and far-red light caused significant disruption of mitochondrial bioenergetic and respiratory functions in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
source: Together, these data show that the combination of MG2I and far-red light caused significant disruption of mitochondrial bioenergetic and respiratory functions in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by ATP measurements (Figure 4A), oxygen consumption data (Figure 4C-G), and lack of compensatory glycolysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claim: If light exposure fully disrupted cellular respiration in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I cells, eno2-expressing neurons account for nearly 25% of the baseline oxygen consumption in an immobilized zebrafish larva.
source: If it is presumed that light exposure fully disrupted cellular respiration in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I cells, it can be inferred that eno2-expressing neurons account for nearly 25% of the baseline O2 consumption in an immobilized zebrafish larva.
evidence: This inference is stated in the discussion and is based on the 24% decrease in whole larval oxygen consumption observed in Figure 4D.

claim: The overall 10% decrease in whole-animal ATP levels suggests a much larger ATP deficit in eno2-expressing neurons.
source: The overall 10% decrease in whole-animal ATP levels suggests a much larger ATP deficit in eno2-expressing neurons that comprise a relatively small fraction of the total cells in a larval zebrafish.
evidence: This inference is stated in the discussion and is based on the 10% whole-animal ATP decrease (Figure 4A) and the fact that eno2-expressing neurons are a small fraction of total cells.

claim: Up to 50% energy expenditure in neurons is devoted to maintaining the transmembrane ionic gradients underlying the resting membrane potential.
source: It has been estimated that up to 50% energy expenditure in neurons is devoted to maintaining the transmembrane ionic gradients underlying the resting membrane potential (Howarth et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Howarth et al., 2012.

claim: Progressive depolarization of NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons during light exposure was rescued by phosphocreatine.
source: Progressive depolarization of NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons during light exposure was rescued by phosphocreatine, a substrate for creatine kinase (CK) that allows ATP generation from ADP, independent of oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by electrophysiology data in Figure 3A-D showing prevention of depolarization with phosphocreatine.

claim: Loss of neural function in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish was attributable to bioenergetic crisis.
source: This observation formally establishes that loss of neural function in this model was attributable to bioenergetic crisis and highlights the importance of mitochondrial respiration for providing the ATP necessary for physiological functions such as active ion transport in neurons.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the discussion and is supported by the rescue of neuronal depolarization by phosphocreatine (Figure 3), which provides ATP independent of mitochondria.

claim: The preservation of creatine kinase function in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish neurons suggests that singlet oxygen-mediated damage did not inactivate cytoplasmic creatine kinase isoforms.
source: The preservation of CK function in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish neurons sufficient to allow rescue of cellular bioenergetics by phosphocreatine suggests that 1O2-mediated damage did not inactivate cytoplasmic CK isoforms, even in the presence of severe mitochondrial disruption.
evidence: This inference is stated in the discussion and is based on the successful rescue by phosphocreatine (Figure 3), which requires functional creatine kinase.

claim: The persistence of acute neurobehavioral deficits in the days following light exposure was attributable to cell death.
source: The persistence of acute neurobehavioral deficits in the days following light exposure was attributable to cell death.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by acridine orange labeling showing increased cell death (Figure 6C-D) and persistent motor deficits (Figure 6A).

claim: Cell death was maximal 24 hr after light exposure.
source: This was maximal 24 hr after light exposure, well after acute neurobehavioral changes were first observed.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by acridine orange quantification in Figure 6D showing peak cell death at 24 hours.

claim: At 24 hr post-exposure, over 30-fold more acridine orange-labeled cells were found in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae than controls.
source: At this time point, over 30-fold more AO-labeled cells were found in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I larvae than controls (WT-MG2I, 9.7 ± 0.8; NeuMitoFAP, 9.7 ± 1.1; NeuMitoFAP-MG2I, 311.7 ± 14.8 AO cells/spinal cord; p<10−15 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I vs. NeuMitoFAP, p<10−15 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I vs. MG2I, p<10−15 NeuMitoFAP-MG2I at 24 hr vs. baseline, 2-way ANOVA with Tukey multiple comparisons test; Figure 6C, D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by acridine orange quantification in Figure 6D.

claim: Prior to far-red light exposure, NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons showed normal morphology with homogenous nuclei, prominent nucleoli and elongated mitochondria with densely packed cristae.
source: Prior to far-red light exposure, NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons showed normal morphology with homogenous nuclei, prominent nucleoli and elongated mitochondria with densely packed cristae.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (pre-exposure).

claim: Immediately after far-red light exposure, severe and widespread mitochondrial abnormalities were observed in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons.
source: Immediately after far-red light exposure, severe and widepread mitochondrial abnormalities were observed in neurons, as described above.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (0 hours post-exposure) and Figure 5E-G.

claim: Despite dramatic mitochondrial changes immediately after light exposure, the adjacent nuclear membrane, Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum appeared normal.
source: Remarkably, however, despite these dramatic mitochondrial changes, the adjacent nuclear membrane, Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum appeared normal at this time point.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (0 hours post-exposure) showing normal cellular structures adjacent to damaged mitochondria.

claim: By 2 hr post-exposure, scattered neurons started to show nuclear chromatin condensation and other morphological changes, including nuclear membrane separation.
source: By 2 hr post-exposure, scattered neurons started to show nuclear chromatin condensation and other morphological changes, including nuclear membrane separation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (2 hours post-exposure).

claim: At 24 hr post-exposure, numerous apoptotic bodies were visible in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons.
source: At 24 hr post-exposure, numerous apoptotic bodies were visible, along with neurons showing morphological features suggesting ongoing apoptosis, and other neurons showing signs suggestive of necrosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (24 hours post-exposure).

claim: At 24 hr post-exposure, neurons showed morphological features suggesting both ongoing apoptosis and necrosis.
source: At 24 hr post-exposure, numerous apoptotic bodies were visible, along with neurons showing morphological features suggesting ongoing apoptosis, and other neurons showing signs suggestive of necrosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (24 hours post-exposure).

claim: The observed phenotypes were caused by singlet oxygen.
source: The requirement of all three components of the chemoptogenetic system (dL5**, MG2I and far-red light) shows that the observed phenotypes were caused by singlet oxygen.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the discussion and is inferred from the requirement of all three components (Figure 2) and the known photochemistry of the dL5**-MG2I system.

claim: The subcellular localization of dL5**-mCerulean3 in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish resulted in spatially-restricted singlet oxygen production within neuronal mitochondria.
source: The subcellular localization of the dL5**-mCerulean3 fusion protein in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish resulted in spatially-restricted 1O2 production within neuronal mitochondria.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the discussion and is supported by the mitochondrial localization of dL5**-mCerulean3 (Figure 1E-G) and the short diffusion radius of singlet oxygen.

claim: Initial damage was confined to mitochondria, as evidenced by preservation of cellular ultrastructure immediately adjacent to severely damaged mitochondria directly after light exposure.
source: Correspondingly, initial damage was confined to mitochondria, as evidenced by preservation of cellular ultrastructure immediately adjacent to severely damaged mitochondria directly after light exposure.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the discussion and is supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 6E (0 hours) showing normal cellular structures adjacent to damaged mitochondria.

claim: In cultured HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-mCerulean3, exposure to MG2I and far-red light decreased the activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III and IV.
source: In cultured HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-mCerulean3, exposure to MG2I and far-red light decreased the activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III and IV (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: COX4 and COX8 encode subunits of complex IV (cytochrome C oxidase).
source: COX4 and COX8 encode subunits of complex IV (CIV, cytochrome C oxidase), and it is possible that the fusion protein is directed to CIV by the COX8 sequence remaining after cleavage of the signal peptide.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge about mitochondrial proteins.

claim: Mitochondrial cristae are dynamic structures whose organization strongly influences assembly of respiratory chain super-complexes and electron transport function.
source: Mitochondrial cristae are dynamic structures whose organization strongly influences assembly of respiratory chain super-complexes and electron transport function (Cogliati et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Cogliati et al., 2016.

claim: In HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-mCerulean3, electron transport and respiration following light exposure were more severely disrupted by a secondary wave of ROS produced by damaged mitochondria.
source: In HEK293 cells expressing mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-mCerulean3, electron transport and respiration following light exposure were more severely disrupted by a secondary wave of ROS produced by damaged mitochondria (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Qian et al., 2019.

claim: FAP-MG2I zebrafish showed a large decrease in whole-animal respiration following exposure to far-red light.
source: FAP-MG2I zebrafish showed a large decrease in whole-animal respiration following exposure to far-red light.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by oxygen consumption measurements in Figure 4C-D showing approximately 24% decrease.

claim: The 12 kb eno2 regulatory element is expressed in the majority of CNS and PNS neurons, most strongly in large projection neurons.
source: The 12 kb eno2 regulatory element is expressed in the majority of CNS and PNS neurons, most strongly in large projection neurons such as retinal ganglion cells, reticulospinal neurons and motor neurons, that are predicted to be most metabolically active (Bai et al., 2007; Bai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Bai et al., 2007 and Bai et al., 2009.

claim: A cysteine residue within the active site of creatine kinase is necessary for enzymatic activity.
source: A cysteine residue within the active site of CK is necessary for enzymatic activity, which has been shown in other experimental systems to be readily inactivated by oxidants including dopamine (Van Laar et al., 2008), superoxide (Yuan et al., 1992) and peroxynitrite (Konorev et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Van Laar et al., 2008, Yuan et al., 1992, and Konorev et al., 1998.

claim: Creatine kinase has been shown to be readily inactivated by oxidants including dopamine, superoxide and peroxynitrite.
source: A cysteine residue within the active site of CK is necessary for enzymatic activity, which has been shown in other experimental systems to be readily inactivated by oxidants including dopamine (Van Laar et al., 2008), superoxide (Yuan et al., 1992) and peroxynitrite (Konorev et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Van Laar et al., 2008, Yuan et al., 1992, and Konorev et al., 1998.

claim: Initial mitochondrial damage provoked delayed loss of cellular viability through secondary mechanisms.
source: We predict that the initial mitochondrial damage provoked delayed loss of cellular viability through secondary mechanisms, several of which may be involved.
evidence: This prediction is stated in the discussion and is based on the observation that cell death peaked at 24 hours (Figure 6D) while mitochondrial damage was immediate (Figure 5E-G).

claim: ATP depletion is a well-recognized cause of cellular necrosis.
source: First, ATP depletion is a well-recognized cause of cellular necrosis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge in cell biology.

claim: The reliance of neuronal ATP synthesis on oxidative phosphorylation may distinguish neurons from cultured cells in their response to mitochondrial damage.
source: In this regard, the reliance of neuronal ATP synthesis on oxidative phosphorylation may be a critical factor distinguishing neurons from cultured cells, which showed compensatory glycolysis and cell cycle arrest, but not loss of viability, following dL5**-MG2I-induced mitochondrial damage (Qian et al., 2019).
evidence: This speculation is stated in the discussion and is based on comparison with HEK293 cells (Qian et al., 2019) which showed compensatory glycolysis, unlike the zebrafish neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claim: Cellular calcium homeostasis was likely disrupted in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons following far-red light exposure.
source: Second, it is likely that cellular Ca2+ homeostasis was disrupted in NeuMitoFAP-MG2I neurons following far-red light exposure.
evidence: This speculation is stated in the discussion and is inferred from the known dependence of calcium homeostasis on ATP and mitochondrial function.

claim: Cytosolic calcium levels are maintained by ATP-dependent transport of calcium into the endoplasmic reticulum and extracellular space, and by mitochondrial calcium buffering.
source: Cytosolic Ca2+ levels are maintained by ATP-dependent transport of Ca2+ into the endoplasmic reticulum and extracellular space, and by mitochondrial Ca2+ buffering that is dependent on the inner mitochondrial membrane electrochemical potential and its structural integrity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge about cellular calcium homeostasis.

claim: Elevated cytosolic calcium can trigger either necrotic or apoptotic cell death depending on severity and subcellular distribution.
source: Depending on severity and subcellular distribution, elevated cytosolic Ca2+ can trigger either necrotic or apoptotic cell death (Pinton et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Pinton et al., 2008.

claim: Compromised mitochondrial structure may allow release of pro-apoptotic mediators.
source: Finally, compromised mitochondrial structure may allow release of pro-apoptotic mediators.
evidence: This speculation is stated in the discussion and is based on established knowledge about mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization in apoptosis.

claim: Cytochrome c is retained physiologically within cristae folds.
source: For example, cytochrome c is retained physiologically within cristae folds; consequently, the obliteration of mitochondrial cristae observed in this model is predicted to allow cytochrome c efflux into the cytoplasm, where it can initiate Apaf-1-dependent apoptosome assembly and activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway (Kroemer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Kroemer et al., 2007.

claim: The obliteration of mitochondrial cristae is predicted to allow cytochrome c efflux into the cytoplasm.
source: For example, cytochrome c is retained physiologically within cristae folds; consequently, the obliteration of mitochondrial cristae observed in this model is predicted to allow cytochrome c efflux into the cytoplasm, where it can initiate Apaf-1-dependent apoptosome assembly and activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway (Kroemer et al., 2007).
evidence: This prediction is stated in the discussion and is inferred from the observed cristae loss (Figure 5E-G) and established knowledge about cytochrome c localization.

claim: Cytochrome c in the cytoplasm can initiate Apaf-1-dependent apoptosome assembly and activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway.
source: For example, cytochrome c is retained physiologically within cristae folds; consequently, the obliteration of mitochondrial cristae observed in this model is predicted to allow cytochrome c efflux into the cytoplasm, where it can initiate Apaf-1-dependent apoptosome assembly and activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway (Kroemer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Kroemer et al., 2007.

claim: It is unlikely that a single downstream mechanism was responsible for the observed cell death.
source: Since morphological markers of both apoptosis and necrosis were visible, it seems unlikely that a single downstream mechanism was responsible for the observed cell death.
evidence: This inference is stated in the discussion and is based on electron microscopy observations showing features of both apoptosis and necrosis (Figure 6E).

claim: The bioenergetic requirements of individual neurons vary according to their morphology and activity.
source: The bioenergetic requirements of individual neurons vary according to their morphology and activity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: dL5** expression varies between different neuronal populations in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
source: Further, dL5** expression varies between different neuronal populations in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish, because the eno2 regulatory element is expressed differentially in discrete cell types (Bai et al., 2007; Bai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Bai et al., 2007 and Bai et al., 2009.

claim: The mechanisms by which neurons die in this model depend on the relationship between bioenergetic demand and loss of ATP.
source: We predict that the mechanisms by which neurons die in this model depend on the relationship between bioenergetic demand and loss of ATP, similar to other cell types (Lieberthal et al., 1998).
evidence: This prediction is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Lieberthal et al., 1998.

claim: A cell with high ATP requirements that sustains a severe mitochondrial injury might undergo necrotic cell death rapidly.
source: For example, a cell with high ATP requirements that sustains a severe mitochondrial injury might undergo necrotic cell death rapidly, whereas less prominent damage in a cell with more modest ATP demands might trigger signaling events culminating in delayed programmed cell death.
evidence: This speculation is stated in the discussion as an example of how bioenergetic demand might influence cell death mechanisms.

claim: Less prominent mitochondrial damage in a cell with modest ATP demands might trigger signaling events culminating in delayed programmed cell death.
source: For example, a cell with high ATP requirements that sustains a severe mitochondrial injury might undergo necrotic cell death rapidly, whereas less prominent damage in a cell with more modest ATP demands might trigger signaling events culminating in delayed programmed cell death.
evidence: This speculation is stated in the discussion as an example of how bioenergetic demand might influence cell death mechanisms.

claim: Targeting neuronal mitochondrial function with dL5**-MG2I provides new experimental opportunities in vivo.
source: Targeting neuronal mitochondrial function with dL5**-MG2I provides new experimental opportunities in vivo, and the tools reported here will be useful for multiple downstream applications.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the discussion and is based on the demonstrated capabilities of the system shown throughout the manuscript.

claim: The dL5**-mCerulean3 fusion protein can be expressed in the mitochondria of any cell type in vivo by crossing Tg(UAS:COX4-COX8-dL5**-mCer3)pt427 zebrafish to a tissue-specific Gal4 driver line.
source: Use of Gal4-UAS genetics will greatly expand the utility of the approach, because the dL5**-mCerulean3 fusion protein can be expressed in the mitochondria of any cell type in vivo, by crossing Tg(UAS:COX4-COX8-dL5**-mCer3)pt427 zebrafish to a tissue-specific Gal4 driver line.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on the established properties of the Gal4-UAS system.

claim: Many relevant transgenic driver lines are available that express Gal4 in dopaminergic neurons or glial cells of interest to disease pathogenesis.
source: Many relevant transgenic driver lines are available that express Gal4 in dopaminergic neurons (Fujimoto et al., 2011) or glial cells (Frøyset et al., 2018) of interest to disease pathogenesis, in addition to larger libraries of enhancer trap Gal4 insertions useful for functional neuroanatomy studies (Bergeron et al., 2015; Kawakami et al., 2010; Marquart et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Fujimoto et al., 2011, Frøyset et al., 2018, Bergeron et al., 2015, Kawakami et al., 2010, and Marquart et al., 2015.

claim: The dL5**-MG2I approach provides improvements on current technology for targeted cell ablation to analyze neural circuits underlying behavior.
source: Furthermore, by exploiting the dependence of neurons on oxidative phosphorylation, our approach provides several improvements on current technology for targeted cell ablation to analyze neural circuits underlying behavior (Bergeron et al., 2015; Godoy et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Bergeron et al., 2015 and Godoy et al., 2015.

claim: The most widely applied method for chemogenetic ablation in zebrafish models relies on metronidazole-induced DNA crosslinking in transgenic animals expressing bacterial nitroreductase.
source: The most widely applied method for chemogenetic ablation in zebrafish models relies on metronidazole-induced DNA crosslinking in transgenic animals expressing the bacterial enzyme nitroreductase (Curado et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Curado et al., 2007.

claim: DNA damage in the nitroreductase model takes many hours, and sometimes days, to accumulate to a level sufficient to ablate targeted cell groups.
source: DNA damage in this model takes many hours, and sometimes days, to accumulate to a level sufficient to ablate the targeted cell groups.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents knowledge about the nitroreductase ablation system.

claim: The rapid light-induced neuronal depolarization caused by mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-MG2I provides temporal certainty regarding lesion onset.
source: In contrast, the rapid light-induced neuronal depolarization caused by mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-MG2I provides temporal certainty regarding lesion onset, avoids pharmacokinetic uncertainties inherent in chemical approaches, and occurs with sufficient rapidity to prevent compensatory changes in circuity that may obscure the resulting neurobehavioral consequences.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on the rapid depolarization observed in Figure 3.

claim: The dL5**-MG2I approach avoids pharmacokinetic uncertainties inherent in chemical approaches.
source: In contrast, the rapid light-induced neuronal depolarization caused by mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-MG2I provides temporal certainty regarding lesion onset, avoids pharmacokinetic uncertainties inherent in chemical approaches, and occurs with sufficient rapidity to prevent compensatory changes in circuity that may obscure the resulting neurobehavioral consequences.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is inferred from the light-based activation mechanism.

claim: The dL5**-MG2I approach occurs with sufficient rapidity to prevent compensatory changes in circuitry that may obscure neurobehavioral consequences.
source: In contrast, the rapid light-induced neuronal depolarization caused by mitochondrially-targeted dL5**-MG2I provides temporal certainty regarding lesion onset, avoids pharmacokinetic uncertainties inherent in chemical approaches, and occurs with sufficient rapidity to prevent compensatory changes in circuity that may obscure the resulting neurobehavioral consequences.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on the rapid onset of effects shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Spatial specificity can be enhanced by directing the activating light to particular neurons or subcellular regions of interest.
source: Furthermore, spatial specificity can be enhanced by directing the activating light to particular neurons or subcellular regions of interest, for example by using a far-red laser beam rather than a diffused light source to excite dL5**-MG2I.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents a prediction about future applications of the technology.

claim: Illuminating individual topological domains of NeuMitoFAP neurons may allow direct exploration of how mitochondrial spatial distribution contributes to maintaining bioenergetic requirements and ionic gradients.
source: Illuminating individual topological domains of NeuMitoFAP neurons may allow direct exploration of how mitochondrial spatial distribution contributes to maintaining bioenergetic requirements and ionic gradients throughout the dendritic arborization, cell body and axonal projection.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents a prediction about future applications of the technology.

claim: Mitochondrial quality control has been implicated in the pathophysiology of neurological diseases including Parkinson's disease.
source: In addition, mitochondrial quality control has been implicated in the pathophysiology of neurological diseases including Parkinson's disease, but the use of chemicals that non-selectively depolarize all mitochondria simultaneously precludes investigation of the underlying mechanisms in specific neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: dL5**-MG2I provides several advantages over other genetically-encoded photosensitizers such as KillerRed.
source: dL5**-MG2I provides several advantages over other genetically-encoded photosensitizers such as KillerRed (Bulina et al., 2006) for these applications, including minimal photobleaching, high quantal yield of 1O2, and excitation by tissue-penetrant far-red light (He et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to Bulina et al., 2006 and He et al., 2016.

claim: The necessity for addition of a chemical fluorogen to photosensitize FAP transgenic animals circumvents practical challenges in generating and propagating transgenic animals expressing constitutively active photosensitizers.
source: In addition, the necessity for addition of a chemical fluorogen to photosensitize FAP transgenic animals circumvents the practical challenges inherent in generating and propagating transgenic animals expressing constitutively active photosensitizers, which must be raised and handled in the dark.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on the chemogenetic nature of the system requiring MG2I addition.

claim: Precision subcellular ablation is likely to have broad applications in neuroscience beyond investigation of mitochondrial function and zebrafish models.
source: Precision subcellular ablation is likely to have broad applications in neuroscience beyond investigation of mitochondrial function and zebrafish models.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents a prediction about future applications.

claim: Future development will include generation of constructs that direct dL5** to other cellular components such as nuclear subdomains, lysosomal proteins or synaptic terminals.
source: Future development of this approach will include generation of constructs that direct dL5** to other cellular components, such as nuclear subdomains, lysosomal proteins or key components of pre- or post-synaptic terminals, allowing resolution of their specific contributions to cellular physiology and pathophysiology.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents a prediction about future work.

claim: The dL5**-MG2I system is fully portable to other experimental systems, including mammalian models.
source: In addition, the system is fully portable to other experimental systems, including mammalian models.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on the general applicability of the molecular components.

claim: At baseline, mitochondria in NeuMitoFAP axons were elongated in shape and distributed regularly along axons.
source: At baseline, mitochondria were elongated in shape and distributed regularly along axons (length 4.89 ± 0.34 μm; circularity 0.29 ± 0.017; number of mitochondria per field of view 75.50 ± 6.84; mean ± SE; Figure 5A-D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with quantitative measurements and supported by confocal microscopy images in Figure 5A.

claim: Mitochondrial length, shape and distribution were unaffected by either far-red light or MG2I alone.
source: Length, shape and distribution were unaffected by either far-red light or MG2I alone (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 5B-D showing no significant changes in control groups.

claim: In the presence of MG2I, an increased number of small, rounded mitochondria were seen in NeuMitoFAP axons immediately following far-red light exposure.
source: However, in the presence of MG2I, an increased number of small, rounded mitochondria were seen in NeuMitoFAP axons immediately following far-red light exposure (length 2.00 ± 0.12 μm, p<0.0001; circularity 0.60 ± 0.014, p<0.0001; number 131.70 ± 10.57, p<0.001; NeuMitoFAP-MG2I post-light compared indivdually with each control group, 1-way ANOVA with Tukey multiple comparisons test; Figure 5A-D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by confocal microscopy images and quantification in Figure 5A-D.

claim: The combination of NeuMitoFAP, MG2I and far-red light caused fragmentation of axonal mitochondria through mitochondrial singlet oxygen production.
source: These data suggest that the combination of NeuMitoFAP, MG2I and far-red light caused fragmentation of axonal mitochondria through mitochondrial 1O2 production.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is inferred from the observed mitochondrial fragmentation (Figure 5A-D) in the presence of all three components.

claim: In the absence of MG2I, neurons in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish showed normal morphology with elongated mitochondria filled with densely-stacked tubular and lamellar cristae.
source: In the absence of MG2I, neurons showed normal morphology; their mitochondria were elongated in shape and filled with densely-stacked tubular and lamellar cristae (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by transmission electron microscopy images in Figure 5E.

claim: In the presence of MG2I, far-red light exposure caused the widespread appearance of lucent areas in neuronal cytoplasm corresponding to swollen, rounded mitochondria with nearly complete elimination of cristae.
source: In the presence of MG2I, far-red light exposure caused the widespread appearance of lucent areas in neuronal cytoplasm at low magnification (Figure 5F, left panel, arrows). These areas corresponded to swollen, rounded mitochondria with nearly complete elimination of cristae (Figure 5F; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by transmission electron microscopy images in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: No abnormal mitochondria were observed in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish prior to far-red light exposure.
source: No abnormal mitochondria were observed in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish prior to far-red light exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 5G showing 0% abnormal mitochondria at baseline.

claim: In the absence of MG2I, a single abnormal mitochondrion was seen immediately following far-red light exposure in NeuMitoFAP zebrafish.
source: In the absence of MG2I, a single abnormal mitochondrion was seen immediately following far-red light exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 5G.

claim: NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish showed 93.3 ± 3.5% abnormal mitochondria immediately post-exposure to far-red light.
source: NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish showed 93.3 ± 3.5% abnormal mitochondria immediately post-exposure, and 97.0 ± 3.0% abnormal mitochondria at 24 hr post-exposure (p<10−15 compared with no chemical control group at same time point; 2-way ANOVA with Šidák multiple comparisons test; Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by quantification in Figure 5G.

claim: NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish showed 97.0 ± 3.0% abnormal mitochondria at 24 hr post-exposure to far-red light.
source: NeuMitoFAP-MG2I zebrafish showed 93.3 ± 3.5% abnormal mitochondria immediately post-exposure, and 97.0 ± 3.0% abnormal mitochondria at 24 hr post-exposure (p<10−15 compared with no chemical control group at same time point; 2-way ANOVA with Šidák multiple comparisons test; Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis and supported by quantification in Figure 5G.

claim: Far-red light exposure in the presence of MG2I caused severe structural deficits in the neuronal mitochondria of NeuMitoFAP zebrafish attributable to damage caused by mitochondrial chemoptogenetic singlet oxygen production.
source: Together, these data show that far-red light exposure in the presence of MG2I caused severe structural deficits in the neuronal mitochondria of NeuMitoFAP zebrafish that were attributable to damage caused by mitochondrial chemoptogenetic 1O2 production.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the results and is supported by the requirement of all three components (Figure 5A-G) and the known photochemistry of dL5**-MG2I.
